content_units: Quarterly Tax Prep Snapshot for an Indian Freelancer
You do not need an exact tax computation yet, but you should keep a clean quarterly record of   income, expense proofs, tax deductions/collections, and compliance documents  .

With   INR 1,200,000 annual receipts from 9 clients   and business expenses of   software/equipment, coworking, and client-related travel  , your recordkeeping should be built to support both   income-tax filing   and   GST/TDS reconciliation if applicable  .
Category   What to track each quarter   Why it matters   Based on your numbers

Client income register   Client name; invoice number; invoice date; service period; amount billed; amount received; payment date; bank reference   Confirms turnover, unpaid invoices, and annual gross receipts     9 clients  , total annual receipts   INR 1,200,000
Invoice archive   Copies of all invoices; credit notes; revised invoices; contract/work order linked to invoice   Supports revenue reporting and disputes   Keep invoice-wise folder by quarter

Bank and payment records   Bank statements; UPI/payment gateway settlements; foreign inward remittance advice if any   Matches actual receipts against invoices   Reconcile every quarter, not only at year-end
TDS documents   TDS deducted by clients; Form 16A; entries visible in AIS/26AS   Prevents missing tax credits   Important if clients deducted tax before paying you

Software and equipment costs   Vendor invoice; purchase date; item description; business-use note; payment proof; warranty/asset record   Helps classify recurring software vs capital items/equipment     INR 180,000   total to categorize properly
Coworking expenses   Monthly invoices/receipts; membership agreement; payment proof   Supports workspace deduction claim     INR 96,000   annual coworking cost

Client-linked travel   Tickets; hotel bills if any; local transport receipts; trip purpose; client/project linked; travel dates   Needed to prove travel was for business, not personal     INR 60,000   directly tied to client work

Compliance and summary file   Quarterly P&L summary; GST returns if registered; advance-tax challans if paid; year-end closing notes   Makes annual filing faster and cleaner   Create one quarter-end review sheet
- Reimbursements from clients, tracked separately from fees
-   Software subscriptions  : design tools, SaaS, cloud tools, productivity apps
-   Equipment/devices  : laptop, monitor, peripherals, storage, accessories
-   Travel for client work  : flights, trains, cabs, mileage logs, accommodation where relevant
Documents to keep attached to each expense
- Split note if partly personal and partly business
- Total invoices raised in the quarter
- Total money actually received in the quarter
Keep these totals quarter-wise as well, so year-end filing is just aggregation rather than reconstruction.
Common Filing and Recordkeeping Mistakes to Avoid
- Mixing   personal and business expenses   in the same claim without a clear split
- Recording only   money received   but not maintaining an   invoice register
- Forgetting to collect   Form 16A   or reconcile   TDS credits
- Claiming travel without documenting   client purpose, dates, and receipts
- Putting all software and equipment into one bucket without checking whether some items should be treated as   assets
- Losing small recurring invoices like coworking add-ons, SaaS renewals, payment fees
- Not reconciling invoices with   bank entries   every quarter
- Ignoring   AIS/26AS   mismatches until filing season
- Treating client reimbursements as normal income without separate tagging
- Failing to retain records long enough for later verification
